sections.title: Slow-storage staging
sections.description: Large data files (e.g. TTTR) on slow or network storage are copied to a fast local cache first, behind a progress bar that shows transfer speed, so the interface does not freeze while reading.

sections.label: Enable staging
sections.description: Copy slow/network files to a local cache before reading. Turn off to always read files in place.

sections.label: Slow below
sections.description: Sources measured slower than this during a short head-read probe are staged locally. Local SSDs read at hundreds of MB/s; network shares are often much slower.

sections.label: Min file size
sections.description: Files smaller than this are always read in place — staging tiny files is not worth the overhead.

sections.title: Plotting
sections.description: A raw per-photon plot (a time trace, a delta-time diagnostic) is thinned above this many points, keeping each bin's minimum and maximum so bursts and dips survive -- a budget, not a hard cap. An already-aggregated plot (a histogram, a correlation curve) is never touched.

sections.label: Max points per plot
sections.description: Raw per-photon plots are thinned above this many points. Raise it on a machine with plenty of RAM and a fast GPU; lower it if a large measurement's plots still lag.

sections.title: Advanced
sections.description: Fine-tuning for the probe and copy loop. The defaults are appropriate for most setups.

sections.label: Chunk size
sections.description: Block size for the probe and copy read loop. Larger chunks reduce overhead but update the progress bar less often.

sections.label: Probe size
sections.description: How much of the file head is read to estimate throughput before deciding whether to stage the rest.
